correctness.rationale: Backward generator equations are invertible at zero and provide exact derivatives E[T] prime = d/(2mu^2) and E[T^2] prime =5d/(2mu^3), hence C prime=d/(2mu). A connected nonfull occupied set has a boundary edge; the probability of n-1 births before deaths tends to one and uniform excursion second moments are O(lambda^-2). Full-occupancy regenerative cycles then have vanishing absorption probability, uniformly bounded second moment and positive mean, so E[T^2]/E[T]^2 tends to two. Singleton entrance occurs with probability 1-o(1) and negligible time; the continuous moment ratio thus has an interior global maximum. The exact two-site calculation and derivative were checked with a standalone rational-arithmetic verifier.

value.rationale: Extinction-time variability, normalized by mean lifetime, quantifies uncertainty in metapopulation persistence independently of units. The result identifies a necessary nonmonotone regime across every connected finite homogeneous landscape from a single founding patch, and the two-site critical ratio is an exact calibration. This is a structural all-network assertion with natural model assumptions, not a narrow or arbitrary parameter slice; it does not claim empirical effect size.
